items.q: How is velocity different from speed?
items.correct: Velocity is speed in a stated direction (a vector); speed has no direction (a scalar).
items.misconception: They are the same thing measured in different units.
items.random_wrong: Velocity is always larger than speed.
items.why: Both use m/s, but velocity includes direction. An object going round a circle at constant speed has changing velocity because its direction changes.

items.q: A spring obeys Hooke's law. How does extension depend on the force applied?
items.correct: Extension is directly proportional to force, up to the limit of proportionality.
items.misconception: Extension stays proportional to force no matter how large the force gets.
items.random_wrong: Extension is inversely proportional to the force.
items.why: Hooke's law (F = kx) holds only until the limit of proportionality; beyond it the spring extends more per newton and may not return to shape.

items.q: A stationary object has several forces acting on it. What must be true?
items.correct: The forces are balanced — the resultant force is zero.
items.misconception: No forces are acting, because it isn't moving.
items.random_wrong: All the forces must point upwards to stop it falling.
items.why: An object can have many forces yet stay still if they cancel — a book on a table has weight down and an equal normal force up: zero resultant, not zero forces.
